Priya (oncall-eng): alert: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-dedicated-42' showing sustained latency p50/p95 spike starting ~1855123400, matched by request 429s and slot exhaustion. SLA pages fired.
Liam (eng-runtime): looking. Is this the same pool we rolled kernel chooser changes to last night? PR #1427 landed in eu-west canary.
Maya (eng-sre): Pager shows quota_used = 102%, pool_slots = 64, active_slots = 64, queue_len -> 200+.
Jon (infra): We had a deployment that bumped reserved_multiplier for some accounts two hours ago. Checking mapping.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime/kernel-chooser v2.3.1 -> eu-west-1 canary at 1855119000, promoted to 25% at 1855119800.
Priya (oncall-eng): root cause hypothesis: either kernel selection regression that reduces throughput per-GPU, or placement/quotas allowing overcommit to single racks -> noisy neighbour. Both would explain saturation.
Liam (eng-runtime): quick profiling snapshot: continuous_batching rate went up 30%, but average tokens_per_batch dropped from 2048 -> 512. That increases scheduling overhead. Also kernel chooser fell back to fallback-kernel for long-context models 60% of time.
Maya (eng-sre): past 10m KV cache hitrate down from 92% -> 61% on the pool, see excerpt: ```
[1855123445] pool=eu-west-1-dedicated-42 kv_hits=61213 kv_lookups=100312 hit_rate=60.97%
[1855123465] active_batches=48 avg_tokens_per_batch=512
```
Nora (eng-ml): fallback-kernel has higher memory pressure -> more frequent KV evictions. If kernel chooser misclassifies sequence_len distribution, the runtime may pick a kernel that thrashes cache.
Jon (infra): I found the quota misconfig: tenant B-ORCH had a legacy multiplier applied twice in the new allocator; they were assigned 12 extra slots on this pool (confirmed). That explains why one tenant is hogging nodes.
Alex (product): tenant B-ORCH is on a paid dedicated plan, but that multiplier shouldn't have applied. Is it a config merge bug?
Liam (eng-runtime): reproduce locally: run load profile with smaller batch tokens triggers fallback kernel selection when sequence_length_threshold=1024 vs model median 896. The chooser condition used `>=` instead of `>`. Off-by-one pushes many requests to fallback.
Priya (oncall-eng): mitigation plan?
Maya (eng-sre): immediate mitigations we did: 1) throttled tenant B-ORCH by temporary rate limit to reduce slot hogging 2) increased pool capacity by 8 slots (emergency bump) 3) rolled back kernel-chooser promotion in eu-west to previous stable commit at 1855114000. That reduced latency quickly (p95 back to baseline in 6m).
Liam (eng-runtime): created hotfix PR to fix chooser inequality and to add a telemetry flag to prevent fallback switch for <5% of traffic during canary. PR #1433.
Jon (infra): removed erroneous multiplier from allocator config and reconciled tenant allocations, tenant now at expected slot count.
Priya (oncall-eng): SLA impact: we breached p99 latency > 3s for ~14 minutes, and some customer requests returned 429s for ~9 minutes. Raising incident to Sev2.
Alex (product): flagging customers affected so CS can prepare messaging.
Nora (eng-ml): action: add a cache-eviction metric to the per-pool dashboard and an alert when kv_hit_rate drops >15% over 5m. Also propose a guard in runtime: if kv_eviction_rate spikes, prefer kernel with lower memory pressure.
Maya (eng-sre): logs we captured for the postmortem: ```
[1855123430] tenant=B-ORCH alloc_slots=24 active_nodes=6 memory_pressure=0.84 kv_evictions=128
[1855123458] scheduler: fallback-kernel chosen model=redwood-llama-4x seq_len=920 avg_batch_tokens=480
```
Priya (oncall-eng): current status: rollback applied, tenant throttled, allocator fixed, hotfix PR open. Monitoring shows p95 back to target. Will keep this thread for postmortem notes.
Liam (eng-runtime): follow-ups for next week: 1) tighter canary ramp guard (traffic% + perf regression checks) 2) add unit test for chooser boundary conditions 3) telemetry for avg_tokens_per_batch and kernel_fallback_rate per-pool.
Maya (eng-sre): ops follow-ups: 1) automated quota audit pre-deploy 2) per-tenant slot anomaly alert 3) capacity surge runbook update.
Priya (oncall-eng): assigning postmortem owner: Liam (eng-runtime) + Maya (eng-sre). Please file PM with timeline, root cause, mitigations within 48h.
Jon (infra): one more note: placement strategy allowed multiple B-ORCH slots on same rack due to affinity override; we need a heuristic to spread heavy tenants. Adding to infra backlog.
Alex (product): thanks team. customers notified. :thumbsup:
Priya (oncall-eng): closing incident channel in 30m if stable. If anyone sees regression reopen here.
